name: Channels
description: Where people reach the agent. Messaging-native agents live in the apps people already use.

name: Triggers
description: What starts a run when nobody is talking to the agent: schedules, heartbeats, events, its own wake-ups.

name: Interface
description: How results are shown. From plain text to generative UI and canvases the agent draws itself.

name: Voice
description: Speech in, speech out, or full-duplex realtime conversation.

name: Devices
description: Hardware and nodes the agent can see, hear or act through.

name: Agent access
description: How other people's agents find and use your product: llms.txt, an MCP server, readiness scores.

name: Harness
description: The agent loop: prompt, call tools, observe, repeat. Owns context engineering, compaction and sessions.

name: Model
description: The reasoning core. Frontier closed models, open weights, or a mix routed per task.

name: Model gateway
description: One endpoint across model providers: routing, fallbacks, keys and spend.

name: Inference
description: What actually runs the weights: hosted providers for open models, or engines on your own hardware.

name: Instructions
description: Files and prompts that tell the agent who it is and how to work: AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, SOUL.md, a system prompt.

name: Multi-agent
description: Delegation: subagents, handoffs, swarms, and agents talking to other people's agents.

name: Built-in tools
description: Actions the loop ships with. Coding agents start from read, write, edit and bash.

name: Web search
description: Live web search and crawling the agent calls as a tool, chosen against each other on quality, speed and price.

name: Sandbox
description: Where the agent's own code runs: your machine, a container, or an isolated microVM in the cloud.

name: Browser & computer use
description: Seeing and driving websites and desktops when there's no API.

name: Tool interface
description: How tools are exposed to the model: MCP servers, OpenAPI specs, plain CLIs, or code the model writes.

name: Connectors
description: Authenticated access to the user's SaaS: Gmail, GitHub, Notion, Salesforce…

name: Payments
description: Letting agents buy things, and get paid, safely.

name: Skills & plugins
description: Procedural knowledge and bundles loaded on demand: skill folders, plugins, slash commands.

name: Memory
description: What the agent remembers across sessions about you and its work. Usually several at once: files, a user model, a graph, an API.

name: Retrieval
description: Search over your own documents and history: vectors, keywords, rerankers.

name: Sessions & files
description: Where sessions, transcripts and the agent's files live.

name: Hosting
description: Where the agent itself lives and runs.

name: Durable execution
description: Long-running work that survives crashes, waits for humans, and resumes.

name: Guardrails
description: Who may do what: graded autonomy, human approvals, pre-action review, injection defence.

name: Identity & secrets
description: Credentials the model never sees, and an identity for the agent itself.

name: Observability & evals
description: Traces, evals and costs, so you know what the agent actually did and whether it got better.
